items.summary: It’s been exactly one month since I published my work porting Greenplum to PostgreSQL 19 and isolating the minimal PostgreSQL core patches needed to run this minimal fork. It all started as a way to extract its ORCA analytical query planner and turn PostgreSQL into a modern, vectorized, high-performance DBMS. And I pulled it off! After a month of development, the database keeps getting faster. I’m now working on a GPU version. Even as a rough draft, on my MSI Raider A18 HX A9W laptop it runs queries faster than LTS ClickHouse: on MergeTree, 1.9x faster by geometric mean and 1.3x by total time, and on vexec_parquet, 13x faster by geometric me…

items.summary: Over the past decade, the timing of PostgreSQL major releases has become very predictable: no earlier than the middle of September, and no later than the middle of October. This year is going to be different. PostgreSQL 19 most likely won’t be released until November, and it’s not impossible that the project could decide to postpone the release further. Moreover, this year, several rather large features were reverted quite late in the beta period: UPDATE/DELETE FOR PORTION OF , SQL Property Graph Queries (SQL/PGQ), and ALTER TABLE … MERGE PARTITION/SPLIT PARTITION were all reverted between August 27 and September 15. While major feature reve…
